bias_targets.methodology: Discussed as an algorithmic artifact of RLHF training where models equate longer answers with higher quality; evaluated and mitigated using length-correction mechanisms in benchmarks like AlpacaEval and WildBench.

Evaluated in synthetic data generation and LLM-as-a-judge setups, where language models are observed to disproportionately favor and score their own generated responses higher than those from other models.
Identified in preference data collection as a cognitive or systemic shortcut where the beginning (prefix) of a completion disproportionately drives the preference label chosen by evaluators.

Evaluated qualitatively by observing model outputs that over-agree with a user's stated beliefs, flatter the user, or validate implausible claims (e.g., a user claiming to be God) at the expense of truthfulness and accuracy.
